subject: Proposal: 18-month term extension + efficiency targets
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Barnes <tim.barnes@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 18-month term extension + efficiency targets

Hi Tim —

Great talking yesterday. As discussed, I put together a practical proposal to cover NovaHealth's next 18 months while locking in material unit-cost improvements tied to predictable commit and a small service-level uplift. High level:

- Term: 18 months (Dec 1, 2027 — May 31, 2029)
- Commit: increase from 1.2B tokens/month to 1.6B tokens/month (flexible ramp in months 1–2)
- Pricing: 7% unit discount on hosted generation tokens if commit is accepted in full; additional 2% credit if we hit the efficiency targets below
- Efficiency targets: implement prefix caching + request routing + model quantization recommendations from our Q3 efficiency audit (we estimate ~12–18% token savings on NovaHealth workloads)
- Overages: monthly true-up at committed unit price; additional burst pool for predictable spikes (configurable)

I attached the Q3 efficiency audit and an initial term sheet so your finance/procurement/legal team have something concrete to review. If you prefer, we can phase the commit (80% month 1, 100% month 2) — Marissa included here can outline the ramp and expected ROI in numbers.

Attachments: q3-efficiency-audit.pdf (PDF, 430KB); RDW-2379-proposed-term-sheet-v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal review by NovaHealth procurement/legal this week
2) We run a short ops call with NovaHealth infra to align on burst/latency SLOs (30–45 minutes)
3) Agree on final term sheet and target sign date (we recommend signing by Nov 12 to lock Q4 pricing)

Let me know what timing works for your team. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive

Subject: Re: Proposal: 18-month term extension + efficiency targets

Irene —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. A few immediate questions from my side and a couple flagged by procurement:

1) Can you confirm how the committed tokens map to the p95 latency SLO? Our clinicians care about sub-200ms p95 for short prompts.
2) What is the mechanics for the additional 2% credit tied to efficiency targets? Is that retroactive or applied to future invoices?
3) Procurement asked about billing cadence — they prefer quarterly invoices for committed spend, is that something you can support?
4) If we exceed the commit in a given month, what’s the guaranteed rate for overage?

We appreciate the proposed ramp flexibility. Before we bring in Legal, I want to make sure the overage economics and SLO language won’t create surprises. Can Marissa provide a usage snapshot and a quick ROI that shows total expected spend under the proposed commit vs current run-rate?

Irene — let’s sync early next week for 20 minutes, maybe Mon/Tue.

Best,
Tim
Director of AI Services
NovaHealth

Hi Tim —

Thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers up front and then a short ROI snapshot attached.

1) Latency mapping: under the proposed commit + our recommended caching configuration, we've measured typical p95 of ~170ms on comparable clinical prompt shapes in Dedicated. For hosted customers with similar volume and the same prefix caching config, p95 sits ~140–190ms depending on shard topology. We will include explicit p95 language in the SLO section of the term sheet.

2) The 2% efficiency credit is applied as a monthly bill credit once the observed token savings vs baseline exceed the threshold for that month. It is retroactive for months in the contract period once the monitoring confirms the sustained savings. We can also do a mid-contract audit cadence (quarterly) if you prefer staged credits.

3) Billing cadence: Redwood supports monthly and quarterly invoicing for committed spend. Quarterly invoice is fine — we can set that in the billing annex.

4) Overages: standard true-up at committed unit price with transparent reporting. For very large, sustained overages we propose a short-term promotion into burst capacity at pre-agreed rates to avoid surprises. We'll include a table in the term sheet.

ROI snapshot (attached):
- Current run-rate (last 90 days): average 1.15B tokens/month, median p95 210ms, estimated monthly spend $72,300
- Proposed commit: 1.6B tokens/month @ discounted rate -> projected monthly spend $65,800 (net of base discount)
- Efficiency lift (caching + batching): estimated token reduction 12% = ~$8k/month saved; combined with commit discount lowers effective unit cost by ~18% vs current run-rate

See attached: usage-breakdown-novahealth.csv and the calculations in the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/rdw/RDW-2379/efficiency-audit

If timeline helps, we can run a short ops alignment next Wednesday (30 minutes) to validate SLOs with NovaHealth infra and then hand to Legal for a focused review.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
